# Requirements Quality Checklist: GitHub Project Status Trigger — Board-Driven Agent Launches

**Purpose**: Validate that the feature's spec and plan are complete, consistent, unambiguous, and testable before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-09-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

These items test whether the requirements are *written* well — complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and fully covering the scenario space — not whether any implementation works. This complements the built-in [requirements.md](requirements.md) (spec-quality gate) by extending coverage to the plan and to gaps surfaced by cross-reading spec + plan.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for how the run is handed the issue body when the body is empty or absent (still a `:ro` file, or skipped)? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-014] — Resolved: Clarifications (task-generation review) + Edge Case "Empty or absent body" — always an empty `:ro` file.
- [x] CHK002 Is a bound specified on the issue-body size written to the read-only file, or is the body written unbounded? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-014] — Resolved: Clarifications — body written unbounded; only the title is capped (256).
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for a board item that is an issue in the target status but carries no Status value edge (null option) versus the matched option? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-004] — Resolved: Clarifications — null Status never matches; dropped like any non-matching option (contracts/github-projects-query.md §4).
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec state the GitHub token scopes/permissions `GITHUB_PROJECT_TOKEN` must hold to read the board? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-016] — Resolved: Clarifications — `read:project` + repo read (or fine-grained Projects/Contents/Issues: read); also in `.env.example` (T001).
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the identity fields when a board item's repository (`owner/repo`) cannot be resolved from the item? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-013] — Resolved: Clarifications — an Issue always resolves `nameWithOwner`; if ever absent the item is skipped defensively.
- [x] CHK006 Is the behavior specified when two agents name the same board but different statuses, given "one shared query per board per tick"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021] — Resolved: Edge Case "Same board, different statuses"; the shared cache stores the whole board and `filter_items` runs per sensor (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §1/§3).
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements defined for what appears in the run record / tags when an optional field (`label`, `repo`) is unset? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-012] — Satisfied: FR-012 fixes the five identity tags from the issue; `label`/`repo` are launch filters only, never tags (data-model.md Run handoff).

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is "within about a minute" quantified with a measurable upper bound tied to `interval_seconds`? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001] — Resolved: Clarifications — within one poll interval (default ≤60s).
- [x] CHK009 Is the source of an item's "first seen" / `entered_at` time defined (sensor poll time vs a GitHub-provided timestamp)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006] — Satisfied: `entered_at = now` = the sensor poll time injected into `plan_tick` (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §2–§3, data-model.md cursor).
- [x] CHK010 Is oldest-first tie-breaking defined when two held issues share the same `entered_at`? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010] — Satisfied: candidates ordered by `(entered_at, number)` — ascending issue number breaks ties (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §2).
- [x] CHK011 Is case-insensitive status matching disambiguated when a board has two Status options differing only by case? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] — Satisfied: a GitHub Projects Status field cannot hold two options differing only by case; case-insensitive match is unambiguous (spec Assumption "Status matching").
- [x] CHK012 Is the 48-character feature-key cap defined as inclusive of the `NNN-` prefix (number + hyphen), so the slug budget is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011] — Satisfied: the whole key (including `NNN-`) is capped at 48 then any trailing hyphen stripped (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §5).
- [x] CHK013 Is the 256-char title cap ordering defined relative to control-character stripping, and is multi-byte-safe truncation specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015] — Resolved: Clarifications — strip control chars first, then truncate to 256 Unicode code points (code-point-safe).
- [x] CHK014 Is "leaves the target status" defined to cover both a move to another status and removal from the board? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008] — Satisfied: "left" = any id in `seen` no longer in the in-status set — covers a move to another status and removal from the board alike (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §2, spec Edge Case "Closed or deleted issue in status").

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK015 Do the feature-key grammar and 48-char cap agree between spec §FR-011, the Assumptions, and plan §Constraints? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Plan] — Satisfied: identical grammar/cap in FR-011, Assumptions, plan §Constraints, and contracts/orchestrator-model.md §5.
- [x] CHK016 Are the five `AGENTBOX_ISSUE_*` env names and five `agentbox/issue_*` tag names stated identically across spec §FR-012/§FR-013 and the plan? [Consistency] — Satisfied: same five env + five tag names in FR-012/FR-013, plan, data-model.md, and `ISSUE_ENV_NAMES`/`ISSUE_TAG_NAMES` (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §1).
- [x] CHK017 Does the `interval_seconds` default (60) and floor (30) agree across §FR-001, the Assumptions, and §FR-023? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001] — Satisfied: default 60 / floor 30 stated identically in FR-001, Assumptions, FR-023, and both contracts.
- [x] CHK018 Is "active from launch until it leaves the status" stated consistently across US3, §FR-008, and the Edge Cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008] — Satisfied: stated identically in US3, FR-008, and the Edge Cases (now also the failed/stuck-run generalization).
- [x] CHK019 Does the run-key definition (`<item_id>:<entered_at>`) in the plan match the spec's exactly-once intent in §FR-006 without contradicting §FR-005 "forgotten on leaving"? [Consistency, Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006] — Satisfied: leaving forgets the id and a re-entry gets a new `entered_at`, so the run key changes only on genuine re-entry — no conflict (contracts/orchestrator-model.md §2).

## Acceptance Criteria Quality & Measurability

- [x] CHK020 Is every functional requirement (FR-001..FR-026) traceable to at least one measurable success criterion (SC-001..SC-010)? [Traceability, Measurability] — Satisfied: SC-001..SC-010 collectively cover FR-001..FR-026 (launch, once-per-entry, one-at-a-time, filters, key, token, resilience, validation, tests); UI FRs traced via US9 acceptance scenarios.
- [x] CHK021 Can "the board token appears in none of the container env, tags, logs, or transcript" be objectively verified as written? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008] — Satisfied: verifiable by inspecting container env, run tags, daemon logs, and the captured transcript for the token value (SC-008, quickstart §6, test T021).
- [x] CHK022 Is there a measurable success criterion covering the UI round-trip / Automation-view behavior (US9, §FR-024..§FR-026), or only acceptance scenarios? [Gap, Measurability] — Satisfied intentionally by US9 acceptance scenarios + quickstart §9 + the UI test suite (T030–T033); UI round-trip is P3 and gated by tests rather than a numeric SC (spec's UI null-action posture).
- [x] CHK023 Is pagination (multi-page board, §FR-021) backed by a measurable success criterion, not just an acceptance scenario? [Coverage, Measurability, Spec §FR-021] — Satisfied: SC-010 requires pagination to be covered by unit tests with paged fixtures (test T024).
- [x] CHK024 Are the load-time validation failures (§FR-023) expressed with objectively checkable message content (names the file and field)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023] — Satisfied: FR-023/US8 require a file-and-field message in the `depends_on`/`checks` style, asserted by test T028.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a daemon restart between emitting a `RunRequest` and the run being recorded (no double-launch, no lost launch)? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-006] — Satisfied: the run key `<item_id>:<entered_at>` plus Dagster's per-sensor run-key ledger dedupe across restarts (FR-006, US2 #2, data-model.md "Restart safety is double").
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for whether the slot stays held when a launched run fails, errors, or is terminated while the issue remains in the status? [Coverage, Exception, Gap, Spec §FR-008] — Resolved: Clarifications + Edge Case "Stuck active feature" — the slot is released only by the card leaving the status, including when the run fails/errors/is terminated.
- [x] CHK027 Is behavior specified for an item that enters and leaves the status entirely between two ticks (never observed in-status)? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-005] — Resolved: Clarifications — never observed in-status, so never launches and never holds.
- [x] CHK028 Do requirements cover both agent kinds (job launched by name, asset materialized) for every launch-path scenario, not only launch? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002] — Satisfied: FR-002/US1 #4 require both kinds; the per-kind `RunRequest` target is asserted by test T006.
- [x] CHK029 Are non-functional/resilience scenarios (GitHub error, rate-limit, timeout, unresolvable board/status/field) each mapped to a defined skip behavior? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, §FR-020] — Satisfied: each mapped in the error table (contracts/github-projects-query.md §5) and asserted by test T024.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK030 Is behavior specified when the same `project_item_id` re-enters the status before the prior run's slot has been released? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-008, §FR-005] — Resolved: Clarifications — impossible; leaving frees the slot and forgets the item in the same tick, so a re-entry is always observed after release.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for an issue that is closed or deleted while sitting in the target status? [Edge Case, Gap] — Resolved: Clarifications + Edge Case "Closed or deleted issue in status".
- [x] CHK032 Is the empty-slug feature-key rule (`NNN` alone, no trailing hyphen) stated unambiguously for titles that are entirely punctuation/emoji/control chars? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-011] — Satisfied: FR-011 + Clarifications (Session 2026-09-17) + contracts/orchestrator-model.md §5 (e.g. `038`).
- [x] CHK033 Is the exclusion of PRs and draft items defined to also prevent them from holding the one-at-a-time slot, not just from launching? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-004, US4] — Satisfied: US4 #3 / FR-004 and `filter_items` drop them before admission, so they never launch and never hold (contracts/github-projects-query.md §4, test T018).

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK034 Are polling rate-limit / API-budget requirements quantified against GitHub limits for the ≥30s cadence and per-board shared query? [NFR, Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Plan §Performance] — Satisfied: plan §Performance bounds it to one shared GraphQL query per board per tick, paginated at 100/page at a ≥30s cadence — a handful of round trips well within GitHub's GraphQL budget.
- [x] CHK035 Are the read-only body file's permissions/mount mode (`:ro`) specified as a security requirement, and is the token's redaction path stated? [NFR, Security, Spec §FR-014, §FR-017] — Satisfied: FR-014 mandates the `:ro` body file; FR-017 + contracts/orchestrator-model.md §6 state the redaction path.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK036 Is the assumption that the spec-013 handoff mechanism can be reused cleanly validated, with its stated fallback (env/tags only, agent fetches body)? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, §FR-014] — Satisfied: Assumption "Handoff reuse (null action)" states the fallback; contracts/orchestrator-model.md §4 confirms the reuse.
- [x] CHK037 Is the dependency on outbound HTTPS egress from the `dagster-daemon` to GitHub documented as a requirement/precondition? [Dependency, Plan §Technical Context] — Satisfied: plan §Technical Context / §Target Platform and quickstart §Prerequisites state the daemon needs outbound HTTPS to `api.github.com`.
- [x] CHK038 Are the "decisions to confirm" all resolved in Assumptions with no remaining `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers, and each labeled as a revisitable default? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions] — Satisfied: the Assumptions section resolves each and labels them revisitable by #22/#23/#24; no `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` remain.

## Traceability

- [x] CHK039 Does every user story (US1..US9) map to at least one functional requirement and at least one acceptance scenario? [Traceability] — Satisfied: every US1..US9 has acceptance scenarios and maps to FRs (US1→FR-001..003/012..015, US2→FR-005..007, US3→FR-008..010, US4→FR-004, US5→FR-011, US6→FR-016/017, US7→FR-019..021, US8→FR-023, US9→FR-024..026).
- [x] CHK040 Is a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme established and used consistently (FR/SC/US references) so items can be traced across spec and plan? [Traceability] — Satisfied: FR-/SC-/US IDs are used consistently across spec, plan, data-model, contracts, and tasks.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied; leave unchecked when a requirement still needs clarification or correction.
- `[Gap]` items flag requirements that appear absent — a satisfied review may resolve them either by adding the requirement or by recording an explicit, intentional exclusion in scope/assumptions.
- Product vocabulary (`triggers`, `on_project_status`, `AGENTBOX_ISSUE_*`, `agentbox/issue_*`, `project_status_<name>`, `GITHUB_PROJECT_TOKEN`) is used deliberately per AGENTS.md as the declarative operator surface, not as implementation detail.
- This checklist complements the built-in `checklists/requirements.md`; it does not replace it. `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
